faq.question: Do I need a visa for Vatican City?
faq.answer: Entry is through Italy, so Italian Schengen rules decide who gets in: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 nationalities are visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa issued for Italy.

faq.question: Do I get a passport stamp for Vatican City?
faq.answer: No official source we read describes a Vatican entry stamp. Entry is through Italy, so any Schengen stamp or EES record comes from the border where you enter the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Vatican City?
faq.answer: Your allowance is whatever your Schengen status in Italy gives you — for visa-exempt visitors, 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area.

faq.question: Will I need ETIAS to visit the Vatican?
faq.answer: Effectively yes, once it becomes mandatory — not for the Vatican itself, but to enter the Schengen Area through Italy on a visa-exempt passport. The fee is EUR 20, and the EU says its ETIAS website is the only official website for submitting applications.
